text:
Maria G: FYI I'm about to hand off in ~15m. We've been getting a bunch of noisy token-latency alerts for the hosted API. Not a full outage but > p95 for a subset of traffic. Thinking to temporarily raise the alert threshold for the next 1h while I finish investigation and handoff. Thoughts? :wave:

Jordan H: thanks for flagging. what's the customer impact? any errors or just latency?

Maria G: no errors, traffic still healthy, but some e2e calls for chat are hitting 1.8s p95 (baseline ~1.1s). Affected only region eu-west-1 and a single model variant (rwd-3b-q8_512). Looks like autoscaler spin/pod eviction noise.

incident-bot: INCIDENT #5128 created · high token-latency · triggered at 2026-02-28T16:12:03Z · perf-impact: partial-degradation · page: oncall-primary

Lee S: ok. if it's localized to eu-west-1 and a specific model, we can route traffic to the next best region/model. But during handoff I'd prefer suppressing noisy pages. Can you summarize what you'll do during the 1h?

Maria G: plan: 1) bump the alert threshold from 1.5s -> 2.0s for 1h, 2) enable temporary routing policy to fallback to rwd-3b-fp16 in eu-west-1 for low-latency tiers, 3) document steps and revert after handoff. I'll run the mute and routing change now and post commands.

Taylor K: please add me as secondary for the next hour. I'll take over if anything escalates.

Maria G: @Taylor K thanks — you're secondary. Jordan, are you ok being remote observer?

Jordan H: yep, I'll monitor dashboards and customer channels.

Maria G: running mute now. command:
```
# mute alert in AlertManager for 1h
/ops alert mute --rule=high-token-latency --duration=1h --reason="handoff temp - eu-west-1 noise"
# apply routing override
/ops route override --region=eu-west-1 --from-model=rwd-3b-q8_512 --to-model=rwd-3b-fp16 --selector=low-latency-tiers --duration=1h
```

oncall-bot: Action recorded: alert mute requested by Maria G (id: am-mute-8273) · routing override queued (id: route-ovr-992)

Lee S: good. make sure the runbook note is in the incident doc and include the exact AlertManager mute ID so we can unmute if needed. Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/latency-incidents

Maria G: added note to incident doc and pasted mute id. doc link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/5128 · mute id: am-mute-8273 · routing id: route-ovr-992

Jordan H: quick customer impact note for handoff: no customer-facing errors, potential slow responses for <10% of EU latency-sensitive requests. Communicated to CX on standby.

Taylor K: got it. if latency drops back to baseline before end of hour we should revert early. Who will run the unmute?

Maria G: I'll unmute before I leave if all green. If I'm gone, Taylor you have perms to unmute (ops role). Steps in runbook.

incident-bot: INCIDENT #5128 status updated · severity: mitigated (partial) · reason: routing override + alert threshold bump · updated at 2026-02-28T16:24:57Z

Lee S: small nit — log the exact metric windows you used to pick 2.0s so we have baseline for postmortem: p95 over last 30m = 1.78s, 5m spikes to 1.9-2.1s.

Maria G: logged metrics and will include a short blameless summary in the incident doc. Thanks team — handing off now. Taylor you're primary in the next hour. I'll be reachable via DM. :thumbsup:

Taylor K: acknowledged. taking primary. if pages resume with errors escalate to P1 and ping oncall-sre.

Jordan H: noted. will update dashboards and notify CX if anything changes.

oncall-bot: Handoff recorded: Maria G -> Taylor K · primary window 2026-02-28T16:30:00Z - 2026-02-28T17:30:00Z · reminder will ping Taylor in 30m

Maria G: final: please remember to revert routing overrides and unmute alerts before closing incident. Also set a follow-up eval to check if quantization profile for rwd-3b-q8_512 is triggering higher latency under short bursts.

Taylor K: will do. thanks! :rocket:
